reason: README Step 2 gives a CPU-only ui-tars post-processing quickstart that parses a model response into actions and pyautogui code, with no model download or credentials.
demo: README 'Step 2: Post Processing' - install the ui-tars package and run the Python usage snippet
goal: Install the ui-tars package from this repo's codes/ directory (the package source in the clone) so that `from ui_tars.action_parser import parse_action_to_structure_output, parsing_response_to_pyautogui_code` works. Then run the README usage snippet on the response "Thought: Click the button\nAction: click(start_box='(100,200)')" at 1920x1080, factor=1000, model_type='qwen25vl'; it must print the parsed dict and the generated pyautogui code. Write /work/env.sh so that it activates the environment where this works.
check: The hidden test confirms the installed parser is the repo's own, then runs it on several action strings (click, type, hotkey, drag, finished) and checks the parsed action types, scaled coordinates and generated pyautogui code.

revision.by: second review (outside the maintained set; independent log check of maintained passes)
issues: Oracle bug: it expects factor=1000 normalisation (0.1, 0.2 -> pixels 192/216) for model_type='qwen25vl', but the parser treats qwen25vl coordinates as absolute pixels on the smart_resize'd 1932x1092 image, giving [0.05176, 0.18315] and pyautogui.click(99.379, 197.802). The repo output is correct per its code.

Goal ambiguity: it allows installing 'from the repo's codes/ directory or PyPI', but PyPI ui-tars is now 0.5.1 (2026-04-09), a different code line whose pyautogui generator divides pixels by scale_factor=1000 (README snippet -> click(0.099, 0.198)). The test must pin the repo's own codes/ package; v2 checks the installed module is byte-identical to codes/ui_tars/action_parser.py.
Coverage widened: v2 also checks the qwen2vl relative path, type/clipboard, hotkey, drag and finished actions.
